questions_and_answers.question: What suffix is added to the infinitive stem to form a German present participle used as an adjective?
Which report in the present participle section discusses letters from Lord Noel‑Buxton?

answers.answer: A report from the German Embassy in Rome
A political report from London to the Foreign Office

questions_and_answers.question: In example 2, what English word best translates the German adjective ‘derartig’?
In the memorandum about the Sudetenland, what was happening to the reports?

answers.answer: They were increasing from hour to hour

questions_and_answers.question: Which noun is modified by the extended adjective construction ‘derartig an Panik grenzenden Erregung’?
According to the article, what should readers do first when encountering an extended adjective construction?

answers.answer: Find the noun to which the modifiers apply
Look up every word in a dictionary

questions_and_answers.question: What does the word ‘Sudetendeutschtum’ refer to?
Which phrase best describes the Labour Party affiliation of Lord Noel‑Buxton?
How does the example about panic describe the level of excitement in England?
What time expression is associated with the increasing reports about incidents in the Sudetenland?

articles.text:
The Extended Adjective Constructions unit introduces present participles and how they form part of extended adjective constructions in German.
The material explains that present participles are formed by adding the suffix -end to the infinitive stem of a verb and can be used as attributive adjectives (e.g., "Die kommenden Wahlen", "Eine dringende Sache").

Example 1 vocabulary and report:
Der Botschafter,- (the Ambassador)
Eingegangen (received)
Der Inhalt (content)
Tschechisch (Czech)
Die Krise,-n (crisis)
Die Wirkung,-en (effect)
Positiv (positive)
Die Äusserung,-en (utterance)
Insbesondere (in particular)
Zu verzeichnen (to be noted)
Die Zuschrift,-en (letter)
Die Arbeiterpartei (Labor Party)
Angehörend (belonging to)

Der Botschafter in London an das Auswärtige Amt
Politischer Bericht
London, den 10. Juni 1938
Eingegangen: 18. Juni
Pol. Ir 1875
Inhalt: Die tschechische Krise, ihre Wirkung auf England.
… An positiven Äusserungen sind insbesondere zu verzeichnen die Zuschriften des der Arbeiterpartei angehörenden betont deutschfreundlichen Lord Noel‑Buxton …

The Ambassador in London to the Foreign Office
Political Report
London, June 10, 1938
Received: June 18
Pol. Ir 1875
Contents: The Czech Crisis, its effect on England…
Among positive utterances are to be noted in particular the letters of the emphatically pro‑German Lord Noel‑Buxton, who belongs to the Labor Party…

Example 2 vocabulary:
Derartig (such a)
Die Panik (panic)
Die Erregung (excitement)

Sentence:
Es bleibt die Frage zu untersuchen, wie es überhaupt zu einer derartig an Panik grenzenden Erregung in England kommen konnte …

Translation:
The question remains to be investigated how it could possibly have come to such a degree of excitement in England, that it borders on panic.

Example 3 vocabulary:
Das Memorandum (memorandum)
Von Stunde zu Stunde (from hour to hour)
Sich mehrend (increasing)
Der Zwischenfall,-e (incident)
Das Sudetenland (Sudetenland)
Beweisen (to prove)
Die Lage,-n (situation)
Das Sudetendeutschtum (Sudeten Germans)
Völlig (completely)
Unerträglich (unbearable)
Die Gefahr,-en (danger)
Europäisch (European)
Der Friede (peace)

Memorandum text:
Die von Stunde zu Stunde sich mehrenden Nachrichten über Zwischenfälle im Sudetenlande beweisen, dass die Lage für das Sudetendeutschtum völlig unerträglich und damit zu einer Gefahr für den europäischen Frieden geworden ist. (Presented to Chamberlain by Hitler)

Translation:
The reports, increasing from hour to hour, concerning incidents in the Sudetenland prove that the situation is completely unbearable for the Sudeten Germans and thus has become a danger to European peace.
